title: Determine the Area of Parallelograms and Rhombuses
objective: I can find the area of a parallelogram using base × height.
model: parallelogram with the base and the dashed perpendicular height, slanted side as distractor, resized with sliders

widgets.component: prerequisite warm-up: rectangle area, perpendicular corner, missing side of a rectangle, equal rows
widgets.root: Keys recomputed (9 × 4 = 36, 90° corner, 48 ÷ 6 = 8, 14 × 6 = 84). 'Perpendicular' is the 5-1 vocabulary term the lesson needs; distractors name the perimeter, added-instead and unit errors.

widgets.component: supported parallelogram area: A = b × h, missing height from the area, 'which measurement is the height', two-row table, error spotted at the substitution step
widgets.root: Keys recomputed (70 sq cm; 54 ÷ 9 = 6 ft; 45 sq cm; table 24 and 33 sq ft; err step 3 turns 7 × 4 into 7 + 4). Item 2.4 names the perpendicular distance, not the slanted side, matching the objective.

widgets.component: match shape to area; two of the six pairs are triangles ('Triangle 8×6' = 24, 'Triangle 10×8' = 40) and the explanation says 'the triangles take the half'
widgets.root: A = ½ × b × h is derived in 5-2 (position 2 of 10). In 5-1 the student has met only the parallelogram and its height; the item both requires the triangle formula and teaches it in its explanation.
widgets.replacement: Replace the two triangle pairs so all six are 5-1 mathematics and two carry a slanted-side distractor: 'Parallelogram, base 8, slanted side 10, height 6' → 48 sq units; 'Rhombus, side 7, perpendicular height 5' → 35 sq units; keep Rectangle 7×3 = 21, Parallelogram 5×4 = 20, Square side 6 = 36, Parallelogram 9×2 = 18. Rewrite the explanation to say 'every shape here multiplies the base by the perpendicular height; the slanted side is never used'. Remove 'triangle rule' / 'halves the product like a triangle's area' from the choice feedback of Practice 2.3 and 5.1 and Challenge 2.6 and 5.1 (they cite a formula that has not been taught); say 'adding or halving the product is not the rule: A = b × h'.

widgets.component: four-row table mixing multiply rows and divide rows, number-line placement of h = 48 ÷ 8, error that substitutes the slanted side
widgets.root: Table keys 126, 7, 8, 90 recomputed (56 ÷ 8, 96 ÷ 12). The number-line hint states the method (h = A ÷ b) but not the value, so the student still divides. 3.4 uses 10 cm slant against 6 cm height.

widgets.where: Practice §4 items 1-6 and Challenge §1 items 1-6, parallelogram variants (gen:areaParallelogram L1-L4)
widgets.component: generated parallelogram word problems with a drawn parallelogram: base, dashed perpendicular height, optional slanted side
widgets.root: Swept 300 seeds at each of four levels: the dashed height is vertical from a vertex to the base with a right-angle mark, a given slanted side is always longer than the height (0 violations), the offset is drawn from sqrt(side² − h²), and L3/L4 'height to the other side' items agree (10 × 4 = 8 × 5). Keys come from the independent check() in tools/studio-gen.test.mjs.

widgets.where: Practice §4.3-4.6 and Challenge §1.1-1.4, rhombus variants of gen:areaParallelogram L2-L3
widgets.component: generated rhombus problems with a drawn rhombus whose side and height are labelled
widgets.root: viz shape 'rhombus' with {side, h} ignores the numbers: assets/studio-viz-geo.js SHAPES.rhombus draws every rhombus with h = 0.78 × side (B = 1.15U, H = 0.78B). The generator produces h/side from 0.21 to 0.85 (about 16% of the L2 draws are more than 0.2 away from 0.78), so a panel labelled 'side 15 cm, height 5 cm' is drawn with a height about 2.4 times too tall. The dashed perpendicular height is the whole lesson, and here its length contradicts its label. Rhombi make up about a third of the L2 and L3 items.
widgets.replacement: In SHAPES.rhombus (the side/h branch, not the diagonals branch) draw to the given numbers: B = side scale, H = clamp(h/side, 0.15, 0.95) × B, offset o = sqrt(B² − H²), keep the vertical dashed height from the top-left vertex to the base, the right-angle mark and the four equal-side ticks. Reject h ≥ side in the generator. Add a check to tools/studio-gen.test.mjs that the drawn polygon's height/side equals dims.h/dims.side within 2% for 300 seeds of areaParallelogram L2-L3.

widgets.where: Practice §4.7 act:sizer L2, Challenge §3.1-3.2 act:sizer L3, L4 (shape para, goal area)
widgets.component: sizer: sliders set the base and height of a parallelogram on a unit grid; formula readout with the student's own numbers; goal hidden
widgets.root: This is the manipulable model: dashed perpendicular height, rectangle ghost overlay, readout b × h with the student's numbers, graded on the measure and on every stated rule. Feedback names the 'added' misconception. L3/L4 use half and quarter steps and 'height is twice the base' style rules.

widgets.component: Connect check: 'What is the area of the parallelogram courtyard?', 'How many tiles does the architect need?', 'Why use the height instead of the slanted side length?' (now carried with the Connect scenario text and the Connect diagram)
widgets.root: The generator now prepends the Connect scenario to each item (ctx), so the givens are on screen, but the figure it attaches is the Connect coordinate plane with only the corner dots plotted: no polygon is drawn, there is no dashed perpendicular height and no right-angle mark (checked by rendering the spec). The student must infer the shape and the height from four unconnected points, which is the representation this lesson exists to teach.
widgets.replacement: Extend diagramToViz (scripts/lib/practice-studio-config.mjs) so a coordinate-plane diagram whose points form a polygon emits "polygon" (point indexes in order) and, for the area lessons, a foot-of-the-height point plus "segments" for the dashed perpendicular. Exact spec for this lesson: {"t":"coord","xmin":0,"xmax":22,"ymin":0,"ymax":22,"grid":true,"points":[{"x":0,"y":0,"l":"A (0,0)"},{"x":18,"y":0,"l":"B (18,0)"},{"x":20,"y":10,"l":"C (20,10)"},{"x":2,"y":10,"l":"D (2,10)"},{"x":2,"y":0,"l":"E (2,0)"}],"polygon":[0,1,2,3],"segments":[[3,4]]}. Keep the scenario text and the three items.

widgets.component: parallelogram area from a base of 13 in and a height of 5 in with unit distractors
widgets.root: 65 sq in recomputed; the unit distractors (65 in, 65 cubic) trap the unit error. See typography: its explanation prints 'x'.

widgets.where: Challenge §2 items 1-6 and §3.3 (err, wr, num, mc, tbl, mc; match)
widgets.component: multi-step missions: error with slanted side, double-the-height proof, gravel bags, panel under a 6 m ledge, three-terrace table, rhombus, match with slanted-side distractors
widgets.root: Recomputed: 66 sq m; 60 ÷ 4 = 15 bags; 84 ÷ 12 = 7 m > 6 m so it does not fit; 54 + 98 + 65 = 217; rhombus 10 cm side × 8 cm height = 80; match 72, 126, 54, 120. Each item forces the perpendicular height over the slanted side.

widgets.where: Challenge §4 items 1-4 and §5 items 1-6 (err ×3, mc, num, mc, num, num, mc, wr)
widgets.component: detective and boss items: slanted side used as height, unit slip, subtract-for-divide, 'any side can be the base', double-base area, pad comparison
widgets.root: Recomputed: 180, 28 sq ft, 72 ÷ 8 = 9, 12 × 6 = 8 × 9 = 72, 126, 45 sq cm, 72, 135 ÷ 9 = 15, pad 66 vs 64 (Pad 1 by 2). Item 4.4 teaches that either side can be the base with its matching height.

formulaOrder.formula: A = ½ × b × h (triangle), as a 'triangle rule' in Practice §3.2 and in choice feedback

typography: Practice §5.4 explanation prints 'A = b x h = 13 x 5 = 65 square inches' with the letter x for multiplication (lesson and the rest of the studio use ×).
